The Munger Approach to Life, Learning, and Decision-Making芒格主义：生活、学习与决策方法

Despite being largely self-taught, Ben Franklin10Ben Franklin本·富兰克林 was spectacularly successful in such diverse fields as journalism, publishing, printing, philanthropy, public service, science, diplomacy, and inventing. Much of Franklin’s success was due to the essential nature of the man—most especially his appetite for hard work, but also his insatiable curiosity and patient demeanor. Above all, he possessed a quick and willing mind that enabled him to easily master each new field of endeavor he chose to undertake. It is not surprising that Charlie Munger considers Franklin his greatest hero, for Munger is also largely self-taught and shares many of Franklin’s unique characteristics. Like Franklin, Charlie has made himself into a grandmaster of preparation, patience, discipline, and objectivity. He has parlayed these attributes into great success in both his personal and business endeavors, especially in his investing.

虽然主要是靠自学，本杰明·富兰克林10Ben Franklin本·富兰克林（Benjamin Franklin）却在新闻、出版、印刷、慈善、公共服务、科学、外交和发明等众多截然不同的领域取得了惊人的成功。富兰克林的成功很大程度上源于他这个人的本性——尤其是他那种吃苦耐劳的劲头，还有他永不满足的好奇心和从容不迫的性情。最为重要的是，他头脑敏捷、乐于接受新事物，这使他能够轻松掌握自己选择的每一个新的钻研领域。查理·芒格53Charles T. Munger查尔斯·T·芒格（Charlie Munger）将富兰克林视为最大的偶像，这一点也不足为奇，因为芒格主要也是靠自学成才，并且拥有富兰克林的许多独特秉性。和富兰克林一样，查理把自己锤炼成了未雨绸缪、富有耐心、严于律己、客观公正的大师。他把这些特质转化为个人生活和商业事业——尤其是投资领域——的巨大成功。

“Like Benjamin Franklin, Charlie has made himself into a grandmaster of preparation, patience, discipline, and objectivity.”与本杰明·富兰克林一样，查理把自己修炼成了准备、耐心、纪律与客观的大师。

To Charlie, successful investing is simply a by-product of his carefully organized and focused approach to life. Warren Buffett25Warren Buffett沃伦·巴菲特 once said, “Charlie can analyze and evaluate any kind of deal faster and more accurately than any man alive. He sees any valid weakness in 60 seconds. He is a perfect partner.” Why does Buffett proffer such high praise? The answer lies in the markedly original approach Munger applies to life, learning, and decision-making—the principal subject of this overview.

对查理来说，成功的投资不过是他经过精心谋划、高度专注的生活方式的一个副产品。沃伦·巴菲特25Warren Buffett沃伦·巴菲特（Warren Buffett）曾经说过：“查理分析和评估任何类型的交易，都比当今在世的任何人都更快、更准确。他能在六十秒内看出任何确凿的弱点。他是一个完美的合伙人。”巴菲特为何给予如此高的评价？答案就在于芒格运用于生活、学习和决策的那套别具一格的方法——而这正是本概览的主题。

“To Charlie, successful investing is simply a by-product of his carefully organized and focused approach to life.”对查理而言，成功的投资，不过是他那精心组织、专注投入的人生态度的副产品。

A word to the wise before we begin: Given the complexity of Charlie’s approach, what follows is not intended as a how-to lesson for the aspiring investor. Instead, it is a general overview of how he seems to do it. Our goal here is to present the basic outline of Charlie’s approach to prepare you for the voluminous details that follow in the rest of the book. If you are anxious to get to the heart of the matter, the “Eleven Talks” section—presented verbatim in Charlie’s own words—is the best source for exacting how-to advice on a broad range of topics. Here we will content ourselves with a presentation of the general thought processes Charlie employs when considering an investment, followed by an outline of his guiding investment principles.

在我们正式开始前，先给明智的读者一句忠告：鉴于查理的方法极为复杂，接下来的内容并非为有志于投资的读者准备的“操作指南”，而是对他“看上去是怎么做的”的总体概述。我们此处的目标是呈现查理方法的基本轮廓，好让你为书中其余部分大量的细节做好准备。如果你急于直击要害，《十一讲》章节——以查理本人的原话逐字呈现——是就广泛主题获取严谨“操作”建议的最佳来源。在这里，我们只需呈现查理在考虑一项投资时所运用的一般思维过程，以及他核心投资原则的概要，便已足够。

Munger’s “multiple mental models” approach to business analysis and assessment

芒格用于商业分析与评估的“多元思维模型”方法

Charlie’s approach to investing is quite different from the more rudimentary systems used by most investors. Instead of making a superficial stand-alone assessment of a company’s financial information, Charlie conducts a comprehensive analysis of both the internal workings of the investment candidate as well as the larger, integrated ecosystem in which it operates. He calls the tools he uses to conduct this review his multiple mental models. These models, discussed at length in several of the talks (especially Talks /poor-charlies-almanack/talk-twoTwo, /poor-charlies-almanack/talk-threeThree, and /poor-charlies-almanack/talk-fourFour), serve as a framework for gathering, processing, and acting on information. They borrow from and neatly stitch together the analytical tools, methods, and formulas from such traditional disciplines as history, psychology, physiology, mathematics, engineering, biology, physics, chemistry, statistics, economics, and so on.

查理的投资方法与大多数投资者所使用的较为粗浅的体系大不相同。查理不会对一家公司的财务信息作肤浅的独立评估，而是对其投资标的的内在运作机制，以及它所处的更宏大、更一体化的生态系统，进行全面分析。他将自己用来开展这种评估的工具称为“多元思维模型57Multiple mental models多元思维模型”。这些模型在几场演讲（尤其是第二、第三和第四场）中被详尽讨论，它们是收集、处理信息并据以行动的一个框架。它们借鉴并巧妙缝合了来自历史学、心理学、生理学、数学、工程学、生物学、物理学、化学、统计学、经济学等传统学科的分析工具、方法和公式。

The unassailable logic of Charlie’s ecosystem approach to investment analysis: Just as multiple factors shape almost every system, multiple models from a variety of disciplines, applied with fluency, are needed to understand that system. As John Muir observed about the interconnectedness of nature, “When we try to pick out anything by itself, we find it hitched to everything else in the universe.”

查理以生态系统视角进行投资分析，其逻辑无可辩驳：正如多种因素塑造着几乎每一个系统，要理解一个系统，也需要娴熟地运用来自不同学科的多种模型。正如约翰·缪尔56John Muir约翰·缪尔（John Muir）在谈及自然界万物互联时所观察到的那样：“当我们试图把任何一样东西单独挑出来时，我们会发现它和宇宙间的一切都牵连在一起。”

“When we try to pick out anything by itself, we find it hitched to everything else in the universe.”当我们试图把任一事物单独挑出，会发现它与宇宙间万物紧紧相连。

Charlie seeks to discover the universe hitched to each of his investment candidates by gaining a firm grasp on all, or at least most, of the relevant factors comprising both its internal and external environment. When properly collected and organized, his multiple mental models (about 100 in number, he estimates) provide a context, or latticework, that leads to remarkable insights as to the purpose and nature of life. More pertinent to our purpose here, his models supply the analytical structure that enables him to reduce the inherent chaos56Chaos混乱 and confusion of a complex investment problem into a clarified set of fundamentals. Especially important examples of these models include the redundancy and backup system models from engineering; the compound interest model from mathematics; the breakpoint, tipping moment, and autocatalysis models from physics and chemistry; the modern Darwinian synthesis model from biology; and cognitive misjudgment models from psychology.

查理力图牢牢掌握构成投资标的内部与外部环境的所有——或至少大部分——相关因素，从而发现与每一个投资标的牵连在一起的那个“宇宙”。当这些多元思维模型被恰当地收集和组织后（他估计约有100种），便提供了一个背景或者说框架，让人对生活的主旨和本质获得非凡的洞见。与本文宗旨更切近的是，他的模型提供了一种分析结构，使他能够将复杂投资问题固有的混乱56Chaos混乱与迷雾，化简为一组清晰的基本要素。这些模型中尤为重要的例子包括：工程学的冗余与后备系统模型；数学的复利模型；物理学与化学的临界点、倾覆临界时刻和自催化模型；生物学的现代达尔文综合模型；以及心理学的认知误判模型。

“Charlie’s models supply the analytical structure that enables him to reduce the inherent chaos and confusion of a complex investment problem into a clarified set of fundamentals.”查理的模型提供了分析框架，使他能把一个复杂投资问题固有的混沌与纷乱，化简为一组清晰的基本要素。

Multiple mental models多元思维模型

The net result of this broad-spectrum analysis is a heightened understanding of how the many factors affecting an investment candidate blend and link to one another. Sometimes this understanding reveals the existence of second-order, ripple, or spillover effects. Other times the factors employed combine to create enormous “lollapalooza-level” results, good or bad. By applying this framework, Charlie lives in a different world from most investors when it comes to investment analysis. His approach accepts the reality that investment problems are inherently complex, and in a manner more in keeping with the rigors of scientific inquiry than conventional investing, he attacks them with a staggering degree of preparation and broad-based research.

这种广谱分析的最终成果，是让人们更透彻地理解影响投资标的的诸多因素如何彼此交融、相互联结。有时，这种理解会揭示出二阶效应、涟漪效应或溢出效应的存在。另一些时候，所采用的因素相互结合，创造出巨大的、好或坏的“lollapalooza 级别”的结果。通过运用这一框架，查理在投资分析上活出了与大多数投资者迥然不同的世界。他的方法接受了投资问题本质上就极其复杂这一现实，并且以一种比传统投资更契合严谨科学探究的方式，以惊人的准备程度和广泛的研究来攻克它们。

Charlie’s “big ideas from the big disciplines” approach to investment evaluation is certainly unique in the business world—as is its origin. Not finding any existing approach adequate to the task, Charlie painstakingly created his own largely self-taught system. The “self-taught” statement is no exaggeration; he once said, “To this day, I have never taken any course, anywhere, in chemistry, economics, psychology, or business.” And yet these disciplines, especially psychology, form the foundation upon which his system is built.

查理在投资评估中采用的“取自大学科的大思想”方法，在商业世界中无疑独树一帜——其来源同样如此。由于找不到任何现成的方法足以胜任这项任务，查理费尽心力地创建了他那套主要靠自学得来的体系。“自学”这一说法毫不夸张；他曾说：“时至今日，我从未在任何地方修过任何化学、经济学、心理学或商学的课程。”然而，正是这些学科——尤其是心理学——构成了他这套体系得以建立的基石。

It is this signature approach, backed by Charlie’s formidable intellect, temperament, and decades of relevant experience, that have made him the virtuoso of business pattern recognition so valued by Buffett. Like a chess grandmaster, through logic, instinct, and intuition, he determines the most promising investment moves, all the while projecting the illusion that the insight came easily, even simply. But make no mistake: This simplicity comes only at the end of a long journey toward understanding—not at the beginning. His clarity is hard-won, the product of a lifetime of studying the patterns of human behavior, business systems, and a myriad of other scientific disciplines.

正是这套标志性的方法，辅以查理过人的才智、性情和数十年的相关经验，使他成了巴菲特极为看重的商业模式识别大师。他就像一位国际象棋特级大师59Chess grandmaster国际象棋特级大师，凭借逻辑、本能与直觉，判断出最有前景的投资“棋步”，同时营造出一种洞见得来轻松、甚至轻而易举的错觉。但千万别误会：这种“简单”只出现在通往理解的漫长征程的终点——而非起点。他的清晰是来之不易的，那是他毕生研究人类行为模式、商业体系以及无数其他科学学科所结出的果实。

“Charlie’s clarity is hard-won, the product of a lifetime of studying the patterns of human behavior, business systems, and a myriad of other scientific disciplines.”查理的清晰来之不易，那是他穷尽一生研究人类行为模式、商业体系，以及无数其他科学学科所结出的果实。

Charlie counts preparation, patience, discipline, and objectivity among his most fundamental guiding principles. He will not deviate from these principles, regardless of group dynamics, emotional itches, or popular wisdom that “this time around it’s different.” When faithfully adhered to, these traits result in one of the best-known Munger characteristics: not buying or selling very often. Munger, like Buffett, believes a successful investment career boils down to only a handful of decisions. So when Charlie likes a business, he makes a very large bet and typically holds the position for a long period. Charlie calls it “sit-on-your-ass investing” and cites its benefits: “You’re paying less to brokers, you’re listening to less nonsense, and if it works, the tax system gives you an extra 1, 2, or 3 percentage points per annum.” In his view, a portfolio of three companies is plenty of diversification. Accordingly, Charlie is willing to commit uncommonly high percentages of his investment capital to individual, “focused” opportunities. Find a Wall Street organization, financial adviser, or mutual fund manager willing to make that statement!

查理将准备、耐心、纪律和客观列为他最根本的指导原则。无论群体心理如何、情绪如何躁动，也不管“这次情况不同了”这种流行说法多么深入人心，他都不会背离这些原则。当这些特质被忠实恪守时，便产生了芒格最著名的特质之一：不常买卖。芒格和巴菲特一样，相信成功的投资生涯归根结底只取决于区区几次决策。所以，当查理看中一门生意时，他会下非常大的赌注，并通常会长期持有该头寸。查理称之为“坐等投资法”，并列举了它的好处：“你付给经纪人的费用更少，你听到的废话更少，而且如果它奏效，税收制度每年还会多给你一个、两个或三个百分点。”在他看来，持有三家公司的投资组合就足以实现多元化。因此，查理愿意将高得不同寻常的投资资本比例，投到个别“聚焦”的机会上。你去找一家华尔街机构、理财顾问或共同基金经理，看谁愿意说出这样的话！

Given Charlie’s record of success, not to mention Buffett’s endorsement, why aren’t his investment practices more routinely emulated by others? Perhaps the answer is that, for most people, Charlie’s multidisciplinary approach is simply too hard. Further, few investors share Charlie’s willingness to appear foolish by not following the herd. Religious in his objectivity, Charlie is content to swim imperturbably against the tide of popular opinion—indefinitely, if necessary—which is a rare attribute in the average investor. And while this behavior can at times appear simply stubborn or contrarian, that is not the defining characteristic. Charlie is simply content to trust his own judgment even when it runs counter to the wisdom of the herd. This lone-wolf aspect of Charlie’s temperament is a rarely appreciated reason why he consistently outperforms the larger investment community. Indeed, if temperament chiefly arises from inborn tendencies, it may be that hard work, intellect, and experience, regardless of their intensity, are by themselves insufficient to make a great investor like Charlie Munger. As we shall witness throughout the remainder of this book, the right kind of genetically predetermined wiring is needed as well.

既然查理有着如此成功的记录，更不用提巴菲特的背书，为什么其他人没有更经常地效仿他的投资实践呢？也许答案在于，对大多数人来说，查理的跨学科方法实在是太难了。此外，鲜有投资者愿意像查理那样，因不随大流而显得愚笨。查理对客观性的坚守近乎虔诚，他甘愿沉着冷静地逆着大众舆论的潮流游泳——必要时，无限期地逆下去——而这正是普通投资者身上罕见的品质。尽管这种行为有时看似固执或逆反，但那并非其决定性特征。查理只是甘愿信任自己的判断，即便它与群体的智慧背道而驰。查理性情中这种“独狼”的一面，是他能够持续跑赢广大投资群体的一个少有人领会的原因。事实上，如果性情主要来自天生的倾向，那么或许即便付出再大的努力、具备再高的才智和再多的经验，本身也不足以造就查理·芒格这样伟大的投资者。正如我们在本书余下的篇章中将看到的，还需要某种与生俱来、由基因预设的“布线”。

Lone wolf
“Charlie is content to swim imperturbably against the tide of popular opinion.”查理甘愿从容地逆流于大众意见之上。

At the 2004 Berkshire Hathaway annual meeting, a young shareholder asked Buffett how to succeed in life. After Buffett shared his thoughts, Charlie chimed in: “Don’t do cocaine. Don’t race trains. And avoid AIDS situations.” Many would dismiss his seemingly flippant answer as merely humorous (which it certainly was), but in fact it faithfully reflects both his general views on avoiding trouble in life and his particular method for avoiding missteps in investing.

在2004年的伯克希尔·哈撒韦（Berkshire Hathaway）年会上，一位年轻股东问巴菲特如何取得人生成功。巴菲特分享了自己的想法后，查理插话道：“别吸食可卡因。别和火车赛跑。避免染上艾滋病的风险。”许多人会把他这看似轻率的回答当作单纯的幽默（它当然很幽默）而置之一笑，但事实上，它忠实折射出他既对生活中如何避免麻烦持有普遍看法，也对投资中如何避免失误有着独到的办法。

Often, as in this case, Charlie generally focuses first on what to avoid—that is, on what not to do—before he considers the affirmative steps he will take in a given situation. “All I want to know is where I’m going to die, so I’ll never go there” is one of his favorite quips. In business, as in life, Charlie gains enormous advantage by summarily eliminating the unpromising portions of the chessboard, freeing his time and attention for the more productive regions. Charlie strives to reduce complex situations to their most basic, unemotional fundamentals. Yet, within this pursuit of rationality and simplicity, he is careful to avoid what he calls physics envy, the common human craving to reduce enormously complex systems (such as those in economics) to one-size-fits-all Newtonian formulas. Instead, he faithfully honors Albert Einstein’s admonition: “A scientific theory should be as simple as possible, but no simpler.” Or, in his own words: “What I’m against is being very confident and feeling that you know, for sure, that your particular action will do more good than harm. You’re dealing with highly complex systems wherein everything is interacting with everything else.”

通常，就像在这个例子里一样，查理一般会先关注该避免什么——也就是不做什么——然后才去考虑在特定情境下他将采取的积极步骤。“我只想知道我将来会死在哪里，这样我就永远不去那里了”，是他最爱的一句妙语。在生意场上，正如在生活中，查理通过干脆利落地剔除棋盘上那些没有前途的区域，从而赢得巨大优势，把时间和注意力腾给更具成效的地带。查理力求将复杂情境化简为最基本、最不受情绪干扰的要素。然而，在追求理性与简单的过程之中，他小心避开他所谓的“物理学妒忌”——人类那种将极其复杂的系统（比如经济学中的系统）化简为放之四海而皆准的牛顿式公式的普遍冲动。相反，他忠实奉行阿尔伯特·爱因斯坦（Albert Einstein）的告诫：“一个科学理论应当尽可能简单，但不能过于简单。”或者用他自己的话来说：“我所反对的，是过于自信、并且觉得自己确切地知道，你的某个具体行动将利大于弊。你面对的是高度复杂的系统，其中一切都在与一切相互作用。”

Another Benjamin—Graham, not Franklin—played a significant role in forming Charlie’s investing outlook. One of the most enduring concepts in Graham’s The Intelligent Investor is Mr. Market.61Mr. Market市场先生 Usually, Mr. Market is a temperate and reasonable fellow, but some days he is gripped by irrational fear or greed. Graham cautioned the investor to carefully use his own unemotional judgment of value instead of relying on the often manic-depressive behavior of the financial markets. Similarly, Charlie recognizes that even among the most competent and motivated of people, decisions are not always made on a purely rational basis. For this reason, he considers the psychological factors of human misjudgment some of the most important mental models that can be applied to an investment opportunity:

还有另一位本杰明——格雷厄姆（Graham），不是富兰克林——在塑造查理的投资观方面扮演了重要角色。格雷厄姆的《聪明的投资者》（The Intelligent Investor）中最经久不衰的概念之一，便是“市场先生61Mr. Market市场先生”（Mr. Market）。通常，市场先生是个性情温和、通情达理的家伙，但有些日子，他会陷入非理性的恐惧或贪婪之中。格雷厄姆告诫投资者，要审慎地运用自己不带情绪的价值判断，而不要依赖金融市场那往往躁狂抑郁的行为。同样地，查理认识到，即便在最有能力、最有干劲的人中间，决策也并不总是建立在纯粹理性的基础上。正因如此，他把人类误判的心理因素，视为能够运用于投资机会之上最重要的思维模型之一：

Personally, I’ve gotten so that I now use a kind of two-track analysis. First, what are the factors that really govern the interests involved, rationally considered? And second, what are the subconscious influences where the brain, at a subconscious level, is automatically doing these things—which, by and large, are useful but which often misfunction? One approach is rationality, the way you’d work out a bridge problem: by evaluating the real interests, the real probabilities, and so forth. And the other is to evaluate the psychological factors that cause subconscious conclusions, many of which are wrong.

就我个人而言，我已经养成了某种双轨分析的习惯。第一，哪些因素真正支配着所涉及的利益，作理性考量时？第二，在大脑的潜意识层面自动发挥作用、从而形成潜意识影响的因素是哪些——这些影响大体上有用，但常常会失灵？一条轨道是理性，就像你解一道桥梁问题那样：评估真实的利益、真实的概率，如此等等。另一条轨道，是评估那些导致潜意识结论的心理因素，而其中许多结论都是错的。

For more specifics on this topic see /poor-charlies-almanack/talk-elevenTalk Eleven, in which Charlie applies mental models from the field of psychology to illustrate 25 common causes of human misjudgment.

关于这一主题的更多细节，请参见《第十一讲》，查理在那一讲中运用心理学领域的思维模型，阐明了人类误判的25种常见诱因。

Obviously, the methods described to this point can’t be learned in a university classroom or on Wall Street. They were developed by Charlie, from scratch, to satisfy his own exacting requirements. They probably deserve a title of their own, something like “Quickly eliminate the big universe of what not to do; follow up with a fluent, multidisciplinary attack on what remains; then act decisively when, and only when, the right circumstances appear.”

显然，迄今为止所描述的这些方法，是既无法在大学课堂上学到、也无法在华尔街学到的。它们是查理从零开始、为满足自己严苛的要求而发展出来的。它们大概值得拥有一个属于自己的名号，大致是：“迅速剔除那一大片不该做的事；接着，对剩下之事发起娴熟而跨学科的进攻；然后，当且仅当恰当的时机出现时，果断行动。”

Is it worth the effort to develop and adhere to such an approach? Charlie seems to think so: “It’s kind of fun to sit there and outthink people who are way smarter than you are because you’ve trained yourself to be more objective and more multidisciplinary. Furthermore, there is a lot of money in it, as I can testify from my own personal experience.”

发展和坚守这样一套方法，值得付出这份努力吗？查理似乎认为是值得的：“坐在那里，比那些远比你聪明的人想得更透彻，这挺有意思的，因为你训练自己变得更客观、更跨学科。此外，这里面能赚到很多钱，这一点我可以用自己的亲身体验来证明。”

“It’s kind of fun to sit there and outthink people who are way smarter than you are because you’ve trained yourself to be more objective and more multidisciplinary.”坐在那儿、用比那些聪明得多的人更清醒的思路取胜，是件挺有趣的事——因为你训练自己更客观、更跨学科。

Munger’s investment evaluation process

芒格的投资评估流程

As we’ve noted, Charlie doesn’t make a lot of investments. His approach is perhaps best summarized by Thomas Watson Sr., founder of IBM: “I’m no genius. I’m smart in spots, and I stay around those spots.” If Charlie knows anything, he knows his spots: his carefully identified circles of competence. To stay within these circles, he first applies a basic, overall screen, designed to limit his investment field to only “simple, understandable candidates.” As he says, “We have three baskets for investing: yes, no, and too tough to understand.”

正如我们已经指出的，查理做的投资并不多。他的方法或许可以用国际商业机器公司（IBM）创始人老托马斯·沃森（Thomas Watson Sr.）的话来最佳概括：“我不是天才。我只是在某些点上聪明，而我始终待在那些点附近。”如果查理懂得什么，那就是他懂得自己的“点”：他小心翼翼界定的能力圈。为了待在这些圈子之内，他首先运用一道基本的、全局性的筛选，旨在把他的投资领域限定在“简单、易于理解的候选者”上。正如他所说：“我们有三个投资篮：可以投、不能投，以及太难理解。”

fig 62
—
Thomas Watson Sr., founder of IBM老托马斯·沃森，IBM创始人
“I’m no genius. I’m smart in spots, and I stay around those spots.”我不是天才。我只是在某些点上聪明，而我就守在那几点附近。

To identify potential “yes” candidates, Charlie looks for an easy-to-understand, dominant business franchise that can sustain itself and thrive in all market environments. Understandably, few companies survive this first cut. Many investor favorites such as pharmaceuticals and technology, for example, go straight to the too-tough-to-understand basket. Heavily promoted “deals” and IPOs earn immediate nos. Those that do survive this first winnowing are subjected to the screens and filters of Charlie’s mental-models approach. The process is intense and Darwinian but also efficient. Charlie detests placer mining, the process of sifting through piles of sand for specks of gold. Instead, he applies his “big ideas from the big disciplines” to find the large, unrecognized nuggets of gold that sometimes lie in plain sight on the ground.

为了识别潜在的“可以投”候选者，查理寻找的是易于理解、占据主导地位、能够在一切市场环境中自我维持并茁壮成长的商业特许权。不难理解，能通过这第一道筛子的公司寥寥无几。许多投资者的最爱，比如制药和科技行业，便直接被归入“太难理解”的篮子。被大肆推销的“交易”和首次公开募股（IPO）则立刻得到“不能投”的判决。那些确实通过了这第一道筛选的公司，还要经受查理思维模型方法的筛子和过滤器。这个过程严酷而达尔文式，但也高效。查理厌恶“砂矿淘金”——那种从成堆沙子里筛寻金粒的过程。相反，他运用其“取自大学科的大思想”，去寻找那些有时就明晃晃躺在地上、却未被识破的大块金子。

“Charlie detests placer mining. Instead, he applies his ‘big ideas from the big disciplines’ to find the large, unrecognized nuggets of gold that sometimes lie in plain sight on the ground.”查理厌恶淘砂挖金。相反，他运用自己『来自大学科的大观念』，去寻找那些有时就明摆在地上、却无人识得的硕大金块。

Throughout his exhaustive evaluation, Charlie is no slave to a database: He takes into account all relevant aspects, both internal and external to the company and its industry, even if they are difficult to identify, measure, or reduce to numbers. His thoroughness, however, does not cause him to forget his overall ecosystem theme: Sometimes the maximization or minimization of a single factor (notably specialization, as he likes to point out regarding Costco’s discount warehouses) can make that single factor disproportionately important.65Moat护城河

在他详尽无遗的评估过程中，查理绝不是数据库的奴隶：他会把一切相关的方面都考虑在内，无论它们属于公司及其行业的内、外部，即便它们难以识别、衡量或化为数字。然而，他的缜密并未让他忘却整体的生态系统主题：有时，对单一因素的最大化或最小化（他喜欢以好市多（Costco）的折扣仓储店为例谈专业化），会使那个单一因素变得与其自身不成比例地重要。

Charlie treats financial reports and their underlying accounting with a Midwestern dose of skepticism. At best, they are merely the beginning of a proper calculation of intrinsic valuation, not the end. The list of additional factors he examines is seemingly endless and includes such things as the current and prospective regulatory climate; the state of labor, supplier, and customer relations; the potential impact of changes in technology; competitive strengths and vulnerabilities; pricing power; scalability; environmental issues; and, notably, the presence of hidden exposures. (Charlie knows that there is no such thing as a riskless investment candidate; he’s searching for those with few risks that are easily understandable.) He recasts all financial statement figures to fit his own view of reality, including the actual free or owners’ cash being produced, inventory and other working capital assets, fixed assets, and such frequently overstated intangible assets as goodwill. He also completes an assessment of the true impact, current and future, of the cost of stock options, pension plans, and retiree medical benefits. He applies equal scrutiny to the liability side of the balance sheet. For example, under the right circumstances, he might view an obligation such as insurance float—premium income that may not be paid out in claims for many years—more properly as an asset. He especially assesses a company’s management well beyond conventional number crunching—in particular, the degree to which they are “able, trustworthy, and owner-oriented.” For example, how do they deploy cash? Do they allocate it intelligently on behalf of the owners or do they overcompensate themselves or pursue ego-oriented growth for growth’s sake?

查理以一种中西部特有的怀疑态度看待财务报表及其背后的会计。往最好说，它们也仅仅是恰当计算内在价值的起点，而非终点。他额外考察的因素清单似乎无穷无尽，包括：当前与未来的监管气候；劳资、供应商及客户关系状况；技术变革的潜在影响；竞争优势与软肋；定价权；可扩展性；环境问题；以及——尤为重要的——隐性敞口的存在。（查理知道，世间没有无风险的投资标的；他要寻找的是那些风险极少、且易于理解的对象。）他将财务报表上的所有数字重新折算，以契合他自己对现实的看法，其中包括实际产生出的自由现金流或所有者现金、存货及其他营运资本资产、固定资产，以及像商誉这样常被高估的无形资产。他还会评估股票期权、养老金计划和退休医疗福利的成本在当前及未来的真实影响。他对资产负债表的负债一侧同样严加审视。例如，在适当的情况下，他可能会把像保险浮存金——多年内或许都不必作为理赔支付的保费收入——这样的义务，更恰当地视为一项资产。他尤其会超越传统的数字运算去评估一家公司的管理层——具体而言，就是评估他们在多大程度上“能干、可靠、以所有者利益为导向”。比如，他们如何配置现金？他们是否代表所有者进行明智的分配，还是给自己过高报酬，抑或为自我膨胀而盲目追求增长？

“Charlie treats financial reports and their underlying accounting with a Midwestern dose of skepticism.”查理以中西部人特有的那分怀疑，看待财报及其背后的会计。

Above all, he attempts to assess and understand competitive advantage in every respect—products, markets, trademarks, employees, distribution channels, societal trends, and so on—and the durability of that advantage. Charlie refers to a company’s competitive advantage as its moat: the virtual physical barrier it presents against incursions. Superior companies have deep moats that are continuously widened to provide enduring protection. In this vein, Charlie carefully considers competitive destruction forces that, over the long term, lay siege to most companies. Munger and Buffett are laser-focused on this issue: Over their long business careers they have learned, sometimes painfully, that few businesses survive over multiple generations. Accordingly, they strive to identify and buy only those businesses with a good chance of beating these tough odds.

最重要的是，他试图从方方面面——产品、市场、商标、员工、分销渠道、社会潮流等等——去评估并理解竞争优势，以及这种优势的持久性。查理把一家公司的竞争优势称为它的“护城河65Moat护城河”（moat）：即它用来抵御入侵的一道虚拟物理屏障。卓越的企业拥有深而不断拓宽的护城河，以提供持久的保护。顺着这个思路，查理审慎考量那些在长期中会围攻大多数公司的“竞争性毁灭”力量。芒格和巴菲特对这个问题极为聚焦：在漫长的商业生涯中，他们——有时是痛苦地——认识到，能够跨越数代生存下来的企业寥寥无几。因此，他们努力去识别并只买入那些有很大机会战胜这些艰难概率的企业。

Finally, Charlie seeks to calculate the intrinsic value of the whole business and, with allowance for potential dilution, etc., to determine an approximate value per share to compare to market prices. This latter comparison is the fundamental purpose of the whole process—comparing value (what you get) with price (what you pay). On this subject he is famous for his viewpoint that “a great business at a fair price is superior to a fair business at a great price.” Warren Buffett often credits Charlie with convincing him of the wisdom of this approach: “Charlie understood this early. I was a slow learner.” Charlie’s insight helped Buffett move from pure Benjamin Graham–style investing to focusing on great businesses such as The Washington Post, GEICO, Coca-Cola, Gillette,65Geico, Coca-cola, Gilette 盖可、可口可乐、吉列 and others.

最后，查理力求计算出整个企业的内在价值，并在考虑潜在股权稀释等因素后，确定每股的大致价值，以便与市场价格进行比较。后一种比较是整个过程的根本目的——比较价值（你得到的）与价格（你付出的）。在这个问题上，他以这样的观点闻名：“以公道价格买入的伟大企业，优于以绝佳价格买入的平庸企业。”沃伦·巴菲特常常把让他信服这一方法智慧之功归于查理：“查理很早便明白了这一点。我学得很慢。”查理的洞见帮助巴菲特从纯粹的本杰明·格雷厄姆式投资，转向聚焦于《华盛顿邮报》（The Washington Post）、政府雇员保险公司（GEICO）、可口可乐（Coca-Cola）、吉列（Gillette）等伟大企业。

“Charlie’s insight helped Buffett move from pure Benjamin Graham–style investing to focusing on great businesses such as The Washington Post, GEICO, Coca-Cola, Gillette, and others.”查理的洞见，帮巴菲特从纯本杰明·格雷厄姆式的投资，转向聚焦《华盛顿邮报》、GEICO、可口可乐、吉列等伟大企业。

Though extremely thorough, Charlie is able to ignore insignificant detail and the distractions to which others sometimes fall victim. Investment variables, just like all other variables, go through their own process of elimination. By the time he is finished with his analysis, he has reduced the candidate to its most salient elements and achieved a remarkable degree of confidence about whether or not to act. The evaluation, finally, becomes not so much mathematical as philosophical. Ultimately a “feel” emerges, a function of both the analysis itself and Charlie’s lifetime of accumulated experience and skill in recognizing patterns.

尽管极其缜密，查理却能够忽略无关紧要的细节，以及他人有时会沦为受害者的干扰。投资变量，就像所有其他变量一样，要经历它们自己的淘汰过程。等到他完成分析时，他已经把候选者化简为其最显著的要素，并对是否行动获得了令人惊叹的笃定。最终，这种评估与其说是数学的，不如说是哲学的。最终会浮现出一种“感觉”，它既是分析本身的函数，也是查理毕生积累的经验与模式识别技巧的函数。

At this point, only an exceptionally superior investment candidate will still be in the running. But Charlie does not immediately rush out and buy it. Knowing that a necessary companion to proper valuation is proper timing, he applies yet a finer screen, a “prior to pulling the trigger” checklist, which is especially useful in evaluating what he refers to as close calls. The checklist includes such items as: What are the current price, volume, and trading considerations? What disclosure timing or other sensitivities exist? Do contingent exit strategies exist? Are better uses of capital currently or potentially available? Is sufficient liquid capital currently on hand or must it be borrowed? What is the opportunity cost of that capital? And so on.

到了这一步，仍在候选之列的就只剩极其卓越的投资标的了。但查理并不会立刻冲出去买下它。他深知，恰当估值的必要伴侣是恰当的时机，于是他再施加一道更精细的筛子——一份“扣动扳机之前”的检查清单，这在评估他所谓的“势均力敌的抉择”时尤为有用。这份清单包括如下事项：当前的价格、成交量和交易因素是什么？存在怎样的披露时点或其他敏感因素？是否备有应急退出策略？当前或潜在地是否存在更好的资本用途？手头是否有充足的流动资本，还是必须去借？这笔资本的机会成本是多少？等等。

Charlie’s exhaustive screening process requires considerable self-discipline and results in long periods of apparent inactivity. But, as Charlie says, “Hard work is an essential element in tracking down and perfecting a strategy, or in executing it.” For Charlie and Warren, the hard work is continuous, whether it results in current investing activity or not—and usually it does not. This habit of committing far more time to learning and thinking than to doing is no accident. It is the blend of discipline and patience exhibited by true masters of a craft: an uncompromising commitment to “properly playing the hand.” Like world-class bridge player Richard Zeckhauser,66Richard Zeckhauser理查德·泽克豪泽 Charlie scores himself not so much on whether he won the hand but rather on how well he played it. While poor outcomes are excusable in the Munger–Buffett world—given the fact that some outcomes are outside of their control—sloppy preparation and decision-making are never excusable because they are controllable.

查理那穷尽式的筛选过程需要相当程度的自律，并导致长时间表面上的无所作为。但是，正如查理所说：“勤奋工作是追踪并完善一项策略，或执行它的关键要素。”对查理和沃伦而言，勤奋工作是持续不断的，无论它是否带来当下的投资行动——而通常它不会。这种把远多于行动的时间投入到学习与思考上的习惯并非偶然。它是任何一门技艺的真正大师所展现的纪律与耐心的交融：一种对“把手上的牌打好”毫不妥协的承诺。就像世界级的桥牌选手理查德·泽克豪泽（Richard Zeckhauser）66Richard Zeckhauser理查德·泽克豪泽那样，查理给自己打分，与其说看重他是否赢了这一手牌，不如说看重他打得有多好。在芒格—巴菲特的世界里，糟糕的结果是可以原谅的——因为有些结果不在他们的掌控之中——但草率的准备和决策永远不可原谅，因为它们是可控的。

“This habit of committing far more time to learning and thinking than to doing is no accident. It is the blend of discipline and patience exhibited by true masters of a craft.”把远多于行动的时间投入到学习与思考，这种习惯并非偶然。它是真正的匠人所展现的纪律与耐心的融合。

On those relatively few occasions when all the circumstances are just right and Charlie does invest, he will likely make a large, decisive bet. He does not pick around the edges, take initial positions, or make small, speculative investments. Such behavior implies uncertainty, and Charlie’s moves, few as they are, are anything but uncertain. As he says, he practices “extreme patience combined with extreme decisiveness.” Charlie’s self-confidence is based not on who, or how many, agree or disagree with him but on his ability to objectively view and measure himself. This self-mastery affords him rare objectivity in gauging his actual knowledge, experience, and correctness of thought. Again, we see the important role played by the right kinds of temperamental qualities: self-discipline, patience, calm, independence. Charlie’s level of investment performance is arguably impossible without them.

在那些相对罕见的、所有条件都恰到好处的时刻，当查理确实出手投资时，他很可能会下注巨大、决断果敢。他不会在边缘试探、建立初步头寸，或做些小规模、投机性的投资。这种行为暗示着不确定，而查理那为数不多的举动，绝不确定。正如他所说，他奉行的是“极度的耐心与极度的决断力相结合”。查理的自信并不建立在谁、或有多少人赞同或反对他之上，而是建立在他客观审视和衡量自己的能力之上。这种自我掌控，使他在衡量自己真正的知识、经验和思想的正确性时，拥有难得的客观。我们再次看到，恰当的性情特质扮演着重要角色：自律、耐心、冷静、独立。没有这些，查理所取得的投资业绩水平可谓不可能。

What makes a great business model for Charlie? His recommended reading67Recommended reading推荐阅读 materials provide some guidance. Guns, Germs, and Steel, The Selfish Gene, Ice Age, and Darwin’s Blind Spot all have a certain theme: a focus on the issue of competitive destruction and an examination of why some entities are nevertheless able to adapt, survive, and even dominate over time. When this theme is extrapolated into investment selection, the preferred Munger business emerges: some thrive by outcompeting (xe0 la Selfish Gene) and others by out-cooperating (xe0 la Darwin’s Blind Spot). Once again, we see Charlie’s rich fluency across a broad range of disciplines at work: How many investors ever consider, as Charlie routinely does, such a broad and sophisticated spectrum of factors? To name but a few, he routinely considers factors such as conversion, i.e., how the laws of thermodynamics intersect with laws of economics (for instance, how paper and petroleum become a newspaper delivered to a front door); psychological tendencies and incentives (notably the extreme behavioral pressures they create, both good and bad); and fundamental sustainability over time (the constant and often deadly interplay between positive factors such as moats and the ravages of competitive destruction). Charlie is possibly without peer when it comes to the checklist of atypical investment factors he considers and his deep fluency in the diverse disciplines from which they are drawn.

对查理而言，什么才算伟大的商业模式？他推荐的阅读材料提供了一些指引。《枪炮、病菌与钢铁》（Guns, Germs, and Steel）、《自私的基因》（The Selfish Gene）、《冰河世纪》（Ice Age）和《达尔文的盲点》（Darwin's Blind Spot）都有着某种共同主题：聚焦“竞争性毁灭”问题，并探究为何有些实体仍能适应、存活，乃至随着时间推移占据主导地位。当这一主题被推演到投资选择中时，芒格偏爱的企业便浮现出来：有些通过超越竞争而兴旺（如《自私的基因》所示），有些则通过超越合作而兴旺（如《达尔文的盲点》所示）。我们再次看到查理在广泛学科上的深厚造诣在发挥作用：有多少投资者能像查理经常所做的那样，考量如此宽泛而精微的因素谱？略举数例，他经常考量的因素包括：转化——即热力学定律如何与经济学定律相交汇（例如，纸张和石油如何变成一份投递到家门口的报纸）；心理倾向与激励机制（尤其是它们所创造的极端行为压力，无论是好的还是坏的）；以及随时间推移的根本可持续性（诸如护城河之类的积极因素与竞争性毁灭的摧残之间，那持续不断且往往致命的相互作用）。在查理所考量的非典型投资因素清单，以及他从中汲取养分的各色学科的深厚造诣方面，或许无人能出其右。

Investors
“How many investors ever consider, as Charlie routinely does, such a broad and sophisticated spectrum of factors?”有多少投资者，能像查理这般惯常地考量如此广博而精微的一整谱因素？

An investing principles checklist

投资原则核查清单

We have now examined Charlie’s approach to thinking in general and to investing in particular. In keeping with our intent to observe how he seems to do it, we will recap his approach by using the checklist methodology he advocates. (For Charlie’s own words of wisdom on the value and importance of checklists, see /poor-charlies-almanack/talk-fiveTalk Five.) Note, however, that the following principles are most certainly not employed by Charlie in a one-by-one or one-time fashion as the checklist format might seem to imply. Nor can they necessarily be prioritized in terms of any apparent or relative importance. Rather, each must be considered as part of the complex whole or gestalt of the investment analysis process, in much the same way that an individual tile is integral to the larger mosaic in which it appears.

至此，我们已经考察了查理的一般性思维方法，尤其是他的投资方法。为了与我们“观察他看上去是怎么做的”这一意图保持一致，我们将用他所推崇的检查清单方法，来重述他的方法。（关于检查清单的价值与重要性，查理本人的箴言参见《第五讲》。）然而请注意，以下这些原则查理绝不会像检查清单的形式所似乎暗示的那样，逐一地、一次性地运用。它们也未必能按照任何表面或相对的重要性来排定优先次序。相反，每一条都必须被视为投资分析过程这个复杂整体或“格式塔”的一部分，正如单块瓷砖之于它所在的更大马赛克拼图那般不可或缺。

✓Incorporate an appropriate margin of safety.
✓Avoid dealing with people of questionable character.
✓Insist upon proper compensation for risk assumed.
✓Always beware of inflation and interest rate exposures.
✓Avoid big mistakes; shun permanent capital loss.
✓Objectivity and rationality require independence of thought.
✓Remember that just because other people agree or disagree with you doesn’t make you right or wrong—the only thing that matters is the correctness of your analysis and judgment.
✓Mimicking the herd invites regression to the mean (merely average performance).
✓Develop into a lifelong self-learner through voracious reading; cultivate curiosity and strive to become a little wiser every day.
✓More important than the will to win is the will to prepare.
✓Develop fluency in mental models from the major academic disciplines.
✓If you want to get smart, the question you have to keep asking is “Why, why, why?”
✓Intellectual humility: Acknowledging what you don’t know is the dawning of wisdom.
✓Stay within a well-defined circle of competence.
✓Identify and reconcile disconfirming evidence.
✓Resist the craving for false precision, false certainties, etc.
✓Above all, never fool yourself, and remember that you are the easiest person to fool.
✓Determine value apart from price, progress apart from activity, wealth apart from size.
✓It is better to remember the obvious than to grasp the esoteric.
✓Be a business analyst, not a market, macroeconomic, or security analyst.
✓Consider the totality of risk and effect; look always at potential second-order and higher-level impacts.
✓Think forward and backward: Invert, always invert.
✓Remember that the highest and best use is always measured by the next best use (opportunity cost).
✓Good ideas are rare—when the odds are greatly in your favor, bet (allocate) heavily.
✓Don’t fall in love with an investment—be situation-dependent and opportunity-driven.
✓“Compound interest is the eighth wonder of the world” (Einstein); never interrupt it unnecessarily.
✓Avoid unnecessary transactional taxes and frictional costs; never take action for its own sake.
✓Be alert for the arrival of luck.
✓Enjoy the process along with the proceeds, because the process is where you live.
✓Be fearful when others are greedy and greedy when others are fearful.
✓Opportunity doesn’t come often, so seize it when it does.
✓Opportunity meeting the prepared mind—that’s the game.
✓Recognize and adapt to the true nature of the world around you; don’t expect it to adapt to you.
✓Continually challenge and willingly amend your best-loved ideas.
✓Recognize reality even when you don’t like it—especially when you don’t like it.
✓Remember that reputation and integrity are your most valuable assets—and can be lost in a heartbeat.
✓Guard against the effects of hubris and boredom.
✓Don’t overlook the obvious by drowning in minutiae.
✓Be careful to exclude unneeded information or slop: “A small leak can sink a great ship.”
✓Face your big troubles, don’t sweep them under the rug.

Since human beings began investing, they have been searching for a magic formula or easy recipe for instant wealth. As you can see, Charlie’s superior performance doesn’t come from a magic formula or some business school–inspired system. It comes from what he calls his “constant search for better methods of thought,” from a willingness to “prepay” through rigorous preparation, and from the extraordinary outcomes of his multidisciplinary research model. In the end, it comes down to Charlie’s most basic guiding principles, his fundamental philosophy of life: Preparation. Discipline. Patience. Decisiveness. Each attribute is, in turn, lost without the other, but together they form the dynamic critical mass for a cascading of positive effects for which Munger is famous (the lollapalooza).

自从人类开始投资，他们就一直在寻找能够瞬间致富的神奇公式或简易秘方。正如你所见，查理的优异业绩并非来自什么神奇公式，也不是来自受商学院启发的某种体系。它来自他所谓的“对更好思维方法的持续追寻”，来自通过严谨准备而“预付”代价的意愿，以及来自他跨学科研究模式的非凡成果。归根结底，它归结为查理最根本的指导原则，他基本的生命哲学：准备。纪律。耐心。决断。每一种特质若脱离其他便不复存在，但它们合在一起，便构成了那种动态临界质量，引发芒格赖以成名的级联式积极效应（即 lollapalooza）。

“Charlie’s superior performance doesn’t come from a magic formula. It comes from what he calls his ‘constant search for better methods of thought.’”查理的卓越业绩，并非来自什么神奇公式。它来自他所谓『对更好思维方法的持续求索』。

Finally, a word or two on why this overview of Charlie’s investment philosophy has focused so much on the subject of what to buy and so little on when to sell. The answer, in Charlie’s own words, serves as a wonderful summation of the Munger school of highly concentrated, focused investing described here:

最后，简单说一两句：为何这篇查理投资哲学的概述如此聚焦于“买什么”，却甚少提及“何时卖”。答案用查理自己的话来说，正是对此处所描述的、高度集中而专注的“芒格学派”投资方式的精彩总结：

“If you can buy a few great companies, then you can sit on your ass. That’s a good thing.”如果你能买下几家伟大的公司，那你就可以稳坐不动了。那是件好事。

Like his hero, Benjamin Franklin, Charlie Munger painstakingly developed and perfected unique approaches to personal and business endeavors. Through these methods, and through the development and maintenance of sound, lifelong habits, he has achieved extraordinary success.

和他的偶像本杰明·富兰克林一样，查理·芒格殚精竭虑地发展并完善了用于个人与商业事务的独特方法。通过这些方法，以及通过培养并坚守健全的、终其一生的习惯，他取得了非凡的成功。
